analyzed_vuln.description: `ndpi_free_flow` decides whether the protocol-specific union contains TLS/QUIC state solely from `detected_protocol_stack`, then interprets `flow->protos.stun_ssl.ssl` union bytes as owned heap pointers and frees them. In this PoV, non-TLS protocol metadata has populated the overlapping union while the flow is ultimately marked TLS/QUIC; the bytes at the `tls_supported_versions` slot are therefore a non-allocated wild address. The invalid free occurs at `ndpi_free(flow->protos.stun_ssl.ssl.tls_supported_versions)` (line 6322). The root problem is missing independent ownership/initialization tracking for pointer-bearing members stored in a shared protocol union; protocol classification is not a safe proxy for pointer validity.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A crafted raw IPv4 packet is passed by `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` to `ndpi_detection_process_packet` using a freshly zeroed flow. Its malformed/ambiguous long payload causes protocol-specific parsing to write non-pointer data into the `protos` union while the final detected protocol stack satisfies `flow_is_proto(...TLS)` or `flow_is_proto(...QUIC)`. When the harness immediately calls `ndpi_free_flow`, the overlapping bytes in the TLS `tls_supported_versions` member are nonzero (the PoV's space/0xff-controlled data) but were never returned by an nDPI allocator, so `ndpi_free` attempts to free a wild address and ASan crashes.

args: Investigate the invalid free in ndpi_free_flow at src/lib/ndpi_main.c involving flow->protos.stun_ssl.ssl.tls_supported_versions. Identify the struct/union definition, every allocation/assignment/free of TLS pointer-bearing union fields, and recommend the smallest robust independent ownership tracking fix, including initialization implications and ABI concerns.

The supplied ASan report says a crafted IPv4 packet causes non-TLS parser metadata to populate bytes overlapping the shared protocol union, while final classification becomes TLS/QUIC. ndpi_free_flow then uses detected_protocol_stack as a proxy for whether TLS union pointers are valid and frees tls_supported_versions as a wild address. The flow starts zeroed in fuzz/fuzz_process_packet.c and is freed immediately after packet processing. We need modify only C/C++ source, not harnesses, and should fix ownership at its root rather than special-case the payload. Please inspect src/lib/ndpi_main.c and relevant headers/protocol parsers.
